headline: TSLA +5.83% reclaims $400 mark as Morgan Stanley, Barclays raise Q2 delivery estimates above consensus — Morgan Stanley upgraded Q2 forecast from 373K to 413K citing European + China demand recovery; Barclays projected ~418K; both above prior consensus of 406K; Q2 delivery report due first days of July; market pricing in a beat as TSLA hit $401.84 intraday, first $400+ close since prior run (Morgan Stanley / Barclays / GuruFocus, Jun 29, 2026)

FSD v14 Lite HW3 first impressions overwhelmingly positive — early access users reporting zero interventions on complex routes (Culver City to Hollywood); Electrek confirms RL improvements, parking/unparking, pedestrian interactions, and navigation handling all translate well via model distillation from HW4; 'distilled the intelligence from HW4 V14 into HW3' per release notes; broader rollout to more HW3 customers over coming weeks pending validation (notateslaapp / Electrek / basenor, Jun 29, 2026)

Grok 4.5 enters private beta at SpaceX and Tesla — 1.5T parameter V9 model enters exclusive private testing at Musk's two companies before public release; Musk claims surpasses Claude on key benchmarks; directly accelerates Digital Optimus/Macrohard AI integration: Grok serves as the reasoning 'conductor' layer that commands Tesla's physical AI agent; signals tightening xAI-Tesla operational integration ahead of Q4 2026 Digital Optimus target (Musk on X / xAI, Jun 28-29, 2026)

FSD v14 Lite officially launches for HW3 hardware TODAY (build 2026.20.5.1) — first FSD update for HW3 vehicles in ~14 months; Tesla distilled HW4 v14 intelligence into legacy hardware via model distillation (HW3 has only ~15% of HW4's effective memory bandwidth); includes RL improvements and offline models from HW4 branch; early access rollout live, broader rollout pending validation; Elluswamy's end-of-June timeline commitment fulfilled exactly on schedule; HW3 remains supervised-only — not a path to unsupervised FSD, but validates Tesla's ability to extend its AI4 architecture to a 3M+ vehicle legacy fleet (notateslaapp / Musk on X, Jun 29, 2026)

NHTSA removes mandatory brake pedal requirement for fully autonomous vehicles — FMVSS 135 updated to allow ADS-exclusive cabins without manual brake controls; alternative stopping-distance testing still required; NHTSA Administrator Morrison: 'tearing down pointless barriers to innovative designs while strengthening fundamental safety requirements'; direct regulatory unlock for Cybercab's pedal-free, steering-wheel-free design; largest federal AV equipment rule reform in decades (NHTSA press release, Jun 24, 2026)

Tesla Q2 2026 analyst delivery consensus: 406,024 vehicles (+12% QoQ vs Q1's 358K; +5.7% YoY vs Q2 2025's 384K) — Goldman Sachs raised Q2 estimate to 420,000 citing stronger-than-expected performance; JPMorgan also at 420,000; median estimate 408,609; energy storage Q2 consensus 13.8 GWh (+57% QoQ recovery); full-year 2026: 1,654,808; Q2 deliveries due first week of July; if met, first clear YoY delivery acceleration since 2023 (Electrek / notateslaapp / Goldman Sachs / Tesla IR, Jun 26–27, 2026)

NHTSA closes investigation into Tesla Model 3/Y steering failures — no safety defect found; closes second major regulatory risk item in two months (follows Smart Summon probe closure in April); Tesla's regulatory scorecard markedly improving heading into H2 2026 with Cybercab brake-pedal rule change also landing this week (notateslaapp, Jun 27, 2026)

Tesla Semi spotted with FSD testing equipment in active road test — first documented evidence of Tesla integrating FSD sensor suite onto Class 8 truck; expands FSD's addressable platform beyond passenger vehicles; Tesla Semi production live at Gigafactory Nevada since Apr 30; FSD-equipped Semi would create a new autonomous freight category ahead of competition (notateslaapp, Jun 27, 2026)

Exclusive: Tesla Model Y L launching in North America this fall (Aug/Sep 2026 internal target) — longer-wheelbase Model Y variant produced at Giga Texas; already sold in China; expands Model Y lineup into a new size/price tier; potential H2 delivery catalyst ahead of year-end; source described timeline as internal target subject to testing/production delays (notateslaapp, Jun 2026)

Tesla Giga Berlin adds new factory building + dedicated rail hub; hires 1,000 more workers — second consecutive wave of 1,000-hire expansions; rail hub reduces logistics costs and increases throughput; follows Giga Berlin's record Q1 with 61,000+ vehicles and 20% production increase; signals sustained European volume ramp entering H2 2026 (notateslaapp, Jun 26, 2026)
